dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, how can I help you this afternoon?

Hi, yes, hello, I'm calling about the drain on my street, the storm drain, because Monday I had to walk in the water to get to my car, and today is Thursday and nobody did nothing. Can you hear me? I have you on speaker.
I can hear you, a little echo but that's okay. So you're calling about a storm drain that backed up. Can I get the address first?
Twelve Brewer Street. Fifth Ward, near the corner where it goes low, you know, where the water sits.
Twelve Brewer Street, Fifth Ward, down at the low corner. Okay. And your name?
Judith Gardiner. G-A-R-D-I-N-E-R.
G-A-R-D-I-N-E-R. Thank you, Judith. Tell me what happened.

So the storm, the snow that turned to rain, Sunday into Monday, right? Monday morning I go out, I have to be at work early, and the whole corner is a lake. No way I'm exaggerating. The water is up to the curb, all across, and my car is parked right there. I had to go through it, in my shoes, up to here, just to open the door. Then I drive all day with wet socks.
Oh, that's miserable. So the water was up to the curb at the corner and you had to wade out to your car Monday morning.

Yes. And I want to be clear, the house is fine, okay? I rent the in-law unit over the garage, and no water came inside, not in my place, not in the main house, nothing. This is not about the house. This is the street. The street is the problem.
Okay, so no water in the house at all, it's the street flooding at the corner. Got it. Do you know if the catch basin there was blocked?

Blocked? It's buried. [inaudible] leaves, like this high, all the leaves from the fall, sitting right on top of the grate. You cannot even see the metal. So the water has nowhere to go, it just sits. Since November those leaves are there. Since November! Nobody comes, nobody sweeps, and then it rains and surprise, there's a lake. No way.
Sorry, you broke up a little. You said the leaves were piled up how high?

Like, a big pile, over the whole grate. Completely covered. Sorry, I'm in a closet, the custodian closet at the school, it's the only quiet place, there's a mop bucket right next to me and everything echoes. [crosstalk] No, no, I'm okay, somebody opened the door. Sorry.
That's alright. So the catch basin at the corner is covered over with leaves, and the water couldn't drain. Is there still water standing there now, today?

Less, it went down some, but there's still a puddle and at night it freezes, so now it's ice right where I have to step. Three days. Three days after the storm and the leaves are still sitting there. I drove by this morning, same pile. I'm not happy, you know? I pay rent there, my landlady pays taxes, and we have to walk in the water like, I don't know, like it's normal.

I understand. I'm going to put in a work order for a catch basin backup at twelve Brewer Street, at the corner, leaves blocking the grate, water up to the curb. Let me see what the schedule looks like. [pause] Okay. The crews have been all over the city since Monday with these, but I can get you on for Monday, February second.
Monday? Another four days? And if it rains this weekend, again I'm in the water.
I know it's not what you want to hear. Monday is what I have right now. If something opens up sooner they'll go sooner, but I'm putting Monday on it so it's on the list.

Okay but listen, I want somebody higher to call me. A supervisor. Because this is not one time someone forgot, this is all fall nobody cleaned it. I want somebody to explain me why the leaves sit there for months. Can you do that?
Yes, I can ask for a supervisor to call you back. Let me get a good number for you.
It's my cell. Four oh one, five five five, oh one eight five.
Four oh one, five five five, zero one eight five. Is that right?
Yes. And they can call after three, three thirty, because I'm driving before that, I can't answer.

After three thirty is best. I'll put that in the note. So, I have the work order for Monday, February second, to clear the catch basin at the corner by twelve Brewer, and a request for a supervisor to call you back at four oh one, five five five, zero one eight five, after three thirty, about the leaves not being cleared this fall.
Yes. That's it. And tell them, please, not just the top. Clean it good. If they just move two leaves and leave, no way, it's going to be the same thing.
I'll put that in there too, that the grate's completely covered and you want it cleaned out properly.
Okay. Thank you, Lorraine. Sorry I'm a little, you know. Wet socks all Monday, I'm still mad.
No, I hear you. Hopefully the weekend stays dry for you. Take care, Judith.
Yeah, hopefully. Bye.
